input.question: How do dead pixel fixers work?
input.ground_truth: When these pixel fixers work, it's because the pixel is stuck, and not dead. My understanding of it is, the signal telling the pixel to change color, never reaches the destination. What the fixers do, is change the color rapidly so that the signals are, in a way, forced to the pixel, so over a long period of time (an hour or two, I think) the pixel becomes unstuck, and will function as normal.

Okay! Imagine your screen is like a big grid of tiny lights, kind of like a bunch of tiny flashlights all working together to show you pictures and videos.

Sometimes, one of those tiny flashlights stops working and stays dark forever. We call that a "dead pixel."

A "dead pixel fixer" is like a magic trick that tries to wake up that sleepy flashlight. It works by sending special signals or pictures to the screen, kind of like tapping it or saying, "Hey, wake up!" really loud. Sometimes, these tricks can make the little flashlight start working again.

But sometimes, the flashlight is broken for good, and the tricks don't work. Then, the dead pixel stays dark.

So, a dead pixel fixer is just trying to help that little light turn on again!
